title: Left join sensitive to order of operations with new streaming engine
body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
import random

# Create data for parent_df
parent_data = {
    'id': [random.randint(1, 100) for _ in range(3)],
    'parent_field1': [random.randint(1, 100) for _ in range(3)],
}

# Create LazyFrame instances
parent_df = pl.LazyFrame(parent_data)
child_df = pl.LazyFrame([], schema={"id": pl.Int32(), "parent_id": pl.Int32(), "child_field1": pl.Int32()})
subchild_df = pl.LazyFrame([], schema={"child_id": pl.Int32(), "subchild_field1": pl.Int32()})

joined_df = parent_df.join(
    child_df.join(subchild_df, left_on=pl.col("id"), right_on=pl.col("child_id"), how="left"),
    left_on=pl.col("id"), 
    right_on=pl.col("parent_id"), 
    how="left"
)
joined_df = joined_df.select("parent_field1")

# this is empty
print(joined_df.collect(new_streaming=True))
# this is not
print(joined_df.collect())

# this is not either
joined_df = parent_df.join(child_df, how="left", right_on="parent_id", left_on="id")
joined_df = joined_df.join(subchild_df, how="left", right_on="child_id", left_on="id")
joined_df = joined_df.select("parent_field1")
print(joined_df.collect(new_streaming=True))
```

### Issue description

In the first case (joining the rightmost tables first, then the result with the left one), with new_streaming my left join behaves as an inner join.
In the second case (where I make the joins from left to right) it works as expected.


### Expected behavior

`a.join(b.join(c))` yields same result as `a.join(b).join(c)`

With the old streaming engine or with polars <= 1.22 this was the case and the order in which I made the join did not make a difference.
